text:
María: quick design thread — jumping off last week's run-history spike discussion. i sketched a tiny set of changes for the playground invoke / structured-output area. want quick take before i mock it up in Figma.

María: main goals: make tool-calls and structured outputs easier to scan in compact runs, reduce ambiguity of which schema produced which field, and clarify fallback behavior for missing keys.

María: proposal A — inline schema badges next to each call, 2-line compact card, left column shows `fn name` + status, right column shows a collapsed JSON preview that expands on hover. tiny microcopy under fn name: "Outputs shown as structured fields".

María: proposal B — stacked pills for each top-level field with small icon for type (str/num/obj/array), tapping a pill opens a side sheet with full schema + example. less noisy in timeline but more clicks.

María: proposal C — keep current compact card but add a subtle header row showing `schema version` and `produced-by` + 3-dot menu -> "View example". minimal change, easiest to ship.

Alex: i like A for discoverability. inline schema badges would solve the "which tool produced this?" problem. question: how do we handle long arrays?

Samir: arrays — collapse to a single pill like "array[items] (3)" and let hover preview show first item. avoid rendering huge lists inline.

Jon: accessibility nit: hover-based expansion is not keyboard friendly. any hover affordance needs a focusable alternative (tab to expand). also screen readers should get a short ALT/aria-text for the pill that reads the schema summary.

María: yep agreed on keyboard/focus. updated constraint: expand on focus or click, not on hover-only. add aria-label: "Structured output from <fn name> — 3 top-level fields"

Eve (UX): copy tweak: instead of "Outputs shown as structured fields" maybe "Structured output (fields may map to tool calls)" — clearer on mapping. also for the schema badge label keep it short: e.g., "schema v2 • invoice-parser"

Alex: can we show a tiny failure state inline? e.g., if schema didn't match expected type, show a red dot + tooltip "schema mismatch — see example". helps debugging during evals.

Samir: +1 to the red dot. implementation thought: we already compute a simple match score in backend. if score < 0.7 show warning. this can be wired to the run metadata.

María: rough sketch of the preview JSON we show when expanded (for devs who want to see exact output):

```
{
  "invoice_id": "INV-123",
  "total": 243.50,
  "items": [ { "name": "widget", "qty": 3 } ]
}
```

María: proposal for microcopy in the compact view: first line: `invoice-parser` • `schema v2` • `matched 85%` (matched score optional, linkable)

Jon: another a11y point: the matched score shouldn't be the only signal. add text like "Likely matches expected schema" or "Possible mismatch" — avoid color-only status.

Eve (UX): agree. use icon + short text. examples: ✅ "Matches schema" / ⚠️ "Possible mismatch" / ❌ "No match". also ensure the contrast of the text meets AA.

PlaygroundBot: deploy-preview available at https://staging.playground.redwood/preview/24812 — includes sample run-history card for invoice-parser and keyboard-expanded previews.

Alex: opening preview now. quick notes after 30s: the badge is helpful but feels visually heavy in the densest mode. maybe reduce badge weight in "compact" density and show full badge in "comfortable" density.

Samir: can we make the compact mode truncate the schema name (e.g., `invoice-pars…`) and show full on focus? keeps layout tidy.

María: yep will do truncate + focus reveal. also plan: tests for keyboard nav and screen reader labels. i'll add a checklist to the PR.

María: small question for PMs — do we want to expose the schema match score in public hosted API responses or keep it internal to console? cc @Alex (for prioritization)

Alex: for now internal-only in console. let's surface in dedicated/enterprise where customers asked for debug telemetry, but not public hosted.

Eve (UX): final ask — when a user navigates from run history to the full invocation view, preserve scroll position in the timeline or animate to make it clear which item opened. small animation helps orientation.

Samir: re animation — keep it subtle and provide a preference toggle (reduce motion).

Jon: will draft the aria labels and keyboard flow doc. posting a small checklist in next message.

Jon: checklist:
- every pill is keyboard-focusable (tab)
- expand on Enter/Space and on click
- aria-expanded toggles on expand
- aria-describedby points to short summary text
- color is not the only indicator for match state

María: thanks all. i'll turn this into a quick Figma with A/B/C screens, add Jon's a11y checklist, and ship a preview link. expect PR by EOD tomorrow. :raised_hands: 

Alex: excited. small follow-up — can we add a single-line permalink copy action on expanded preview so engineers can link to the exact invocation? useful when triaging.

María: good call — adding "Copy link to invocation" in the 3-dot menu.

PlaygroundBot: noted: created ticket PDX-3347 "run-history: structured-output badges + keyboard accessible previews" and attached preview URL.
